header: THE EMPLOYEE MANAGER'S OPERATIONS (step 66a; my request, 1 Nov 2026): add, change and delete an employee; authorise and withdraw an executive; read the history. As in the PAX editor's store, I made every operation
- run in ONE transaction, under one lock (two people cannot add the same ticket at the same moment),
- check the person's authority INSIDE the transaction (the HOD of C&IT by SUPERADMIN_TICKETS, or an executive the HOD has authorised and not withdrawn),
- write its audit line in the same transaction: a change cannot be saved without the record of who made it and of the record before and after.

- the two DATES (birth, joining) are the HOD's alone: for anybody else they are neither shown nor changed, in the form and in the history (my rule: "no user can search the dob and doj ... except the HOD");
- only the HOD DELETES a person (it can never be the HOD himself), and he may remove the person's login account with him;
- the table is the live roster, whose exact columns this code does not assume: the optional ones (address, e-mails, the doctor flag, the dates, source_snapshot_date) are DISCOVERED in the database.

THE LOGIN ACCOUNT (step 66b): the mobile number and the general e-mail of an employee are kept in his login account (public."user": contactNo, email: what the search cards mask and reveal), so when I add an employee I also create that account, with his SAIL P.No. as the first password (bcrypt, as the other accounts are); a person who has an account already (the same ticket) is linked, not duplicated. A change keeps the account's name, P.No., designation, mobile and e-mail in step with the roster and NEVER touches the password. The manager never shows a whole mobile number or e-mail: it uses the masks of the search cards. The database is reached through a tiny interface (EmpDb), so the same code runs against the application's connection and against a scratch database in the tests.

doc: LOCK the person's row (and his login account's) BEFORE it is read for a change or a delete. The global write lock every save takes already makes two saves of this manager wait for each other; my row lock closes the gap for any writer that does not know that lock (a SQL script, another program): it has to wait until this transaction ends, and the version check that follows then sees what it did.

symbols.name: SCHEMA_MEMORY_MS
symbols.sig: const SCHEMA_MEMORY_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000
doc: REMEMBERING THE TABLE LAYOUT AND THE CODE LISTS (step 67d; my request, 1 Nov 2026: "speed up saves by remembering the table layout and the code lists for a few minutes instead of reading them on every save"). Every search, add, change and delete used to ask the database first what columns the tables have (discover) and, for add and change, for the whole list of designations and departments (loadLookups): three round trips to Supabase, each about half a second on a development machine, on EVERY save. They change only when somebody runs a migration, so I remember them for 5 minutes, SEPARATELY (the layout and the lists). WHERE: on the database connection (`db.cacheKey`), not in a global: another database, a test database or a restarted server never sees this memory, and a wrapper without a key remembers nothing. WHY IT CANNOT MAKE A SAVE WRONG:
* when a panel opens (the `lookups` request) both are read FRESH and remembered, so what is on the screen is never staler than the moment it was opened;

* a save refused only because a designation or department is not in the REMEMBERED list reads the real list and checks again before it gives up (a designation added by a script a minute ago works at once);
* a designation or department removed since it was remembered is refused by the database (a foreign key): that becomes a clear message, the memory is cleared, and nothing is half written.
I remember only the layout and the codes and titles: nothing about a person, so nothing private.
